summary: Ingenious 3D takes Knizia's classic tile-laying abstract and adds stackable layers, letting players place hexagonal tiles on top of existing ones to open new scoring lines. The core tension is unchanged: you must raise your worst-scoring color rather than maximize your best, keeping matches close and forcing balanced play.
praised: close, tense scoring from the 'raise your minimum' rule
3D layering adds a fresh spatial wrinkle to a familiar formula
criticised: theme-free abstraction won't appeal to everyone
stacking can feel like an add-on rather than an essential change
still largely a multiplayer-solitaire puzzle with limited direct interaction

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with shared tile supply and occasional blocking
interaction.detail: Players draw from a shared pool of tiles and can block or deny opponents' scoring lines through placement, but each player scores on their own board, so most of the game is independent optimization rather than direct conflict.

subsystems: tile-placement pattern scoring across six colors
sources: score total in each of the six colors
scoring.how_you_win: Place stacking tiles to extend lines of matching symbols, scoring in all six colors as you go; your effective score is always your lowest color, so you win by having the best 'worst color' when tiles run out — or instantly if you're the first to max out a color while leading.
